title: Streaming response truncation and client-retry compatibility workaround
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Summary
=======
This playbook explains a common class of customer incidents where streaming responses are cut off mid‑generation and client retries cause partial or duplicate output. The document provides: a reproducible test, short‑term customer workarounds, operational remediation steps for platform/infrastructure, recommended engineering fixes and SDK guidance, and customer communication templates.

Scope
-----
Applies to: hosted Redwood API streaming endpoints (HTTP chunked and gRPC-stream variants) and customer SDKs calling streaming endpoints. It is relevant for customers using: long-context completions (>1024 tokens), streaming websockets, gRPC-web clients behind reverse proxies, and custom sidecars that perform request/response buffering.

Impact and Symptoms
-------------------
- Symptom: client observes stream abruptly end with a partial text chunk; SDK-level retry issues produce either truncated continuation or duplicated tokens.
- Severity: can range from low (minor content loss) to high (broken customer UX, safety-critical truncation).
- Typical customer observable metrics: increased client errors (4xx/5xx), spike in token cost anomalies (retries), and customer support tickets reporting missing or repeated text.

Root causes (common)
--------------------
1) Ingress reverse proxy timeouts closing connections during long generation bursts (e.g., proxy idle or header timeout < generation window).
2) Intermediate gateways or L7 load balancers converting chunked transfer into buffered responses and truncating on upstream disconnect.
3) gRPC-web / browser-side proxies not supporting connection keepalive semantics and dropping streams after a hard idle.
4) Client SDK retry logic that treats streaming disconnect as a full-request failure and replays request without resume semantics or idempotency keys.
5) Missing correlation metadata (request_id / token cursor) preventing server-side resume or deduplication paths.
6) Tokenization boundary issues where the server flushes partial token chunks and a retry repeats the same tokens.

Immediate customer-facing reproduction steps (for support agents)
---------------------------------------------------------------
1. Collect: customer request_id, timestamp, model, prompt length, input_token_count, and the SDK version.
2. Ask customer to reproduce with a small controlled prompt that reliably produces >500 tokens. Example reproducible curl below.
3. Request client logs (network events) and server request logs (ingest events, connection_close reason).

Temporary workarounds (customer-facing)
-------------------------------------
- Short term (recommended): Ask customer to set streaming=false for critical flows while we stabilize the environment. This preserves correctness at the cost of latency and server CPU.
- If streaming is required: request SDK update to the latest version (see below) that enables graceful resume or to enable the ’chunk_keepalive’ option in SDKs.
- Suggest client-side adaptive retry: on stream disconnect, retry using the same request with header X-Redwood-Dedup-Id: <dedup-id> and the optional resume cursor header X-Redwood-Resume-From:<last_token_index> if available.
- For browser customers using gRPC-web: route traffic through a known working proxy (our supported ingress path) rather than custom proxies that rewrite transfer semantics.

Operational remediation (infra / SRE)
------------------------------------
1) Short-term changes (can be applied within 1–2 hours):
   - Increase ingress L7 idle_timeout and header_timeouts to at least 120s for streaming endpoints.
   - Disable buffering on NGINX/Envoy for streaming routes (set proxy_buffering off; use chunked responses).
   - Enable HTTP/2 keepalive and lower active connection resets during long-lived connections.
2) Medium-term (days):
   - Deploy a connection-health probe that emits per-request stream_liveness metrics (events: stream_open, keepalive_ping, client_ack, stream_close).
   - Add server-side telemetry: last_sent_token_index, last_saved_kv_offset, and request_dedup_id to correlation logs.
3) Long-term (weeks):
   - Introduce server resume endpoints: POST /v1/resume-stream with body { request_id, resume_cursor } which replays remaining tokens deterministically.
   - Harden load balancer implementations to preserve chunked transfer encoding and to avoid early truncation under connection recycle.

Engineering permanent fixes and SDK guidance
-------------------------------------------
- Server: persist deterministic generation checkpoints for requests that exceed 512 tokens so a resume can produce bit-identical continuations.
- API: add optional resume metadata in the streaming protocol: final_chunk_offset and generation_checkpoint_id.
- SDKs: ship automatic resume + safe-retry logic: on disconnect attempt Resume flow when checkpoint metadata is present; fall back to non-streaming retried request when not.
- SDK idempotency: always attach X-Redwood-Dedup-Id for any request marked retryable. Servers must honor dedup id to avoid double billing for the same tokens.

Runbook for support & oncall (step-by-step)
------------------------------------------
1. Intake: create internal ticket with severity classification. Fill fields: request_id, customer, model, endpoint, SDK version, time window.
2. Quick triage (5–15 minutes): check ingress metrics for the tenant and last 15m connection resets.
3. Reproduce: ask for a minimal prompt and run reproduction through our supported curl example.
4. Action: if truncation reproduces consistently, apply short-term infra tweaks (increase timeouts, disable buffering) as a canary for the customer.
5. Customer communication: send the short template below (see Communication Templates).
6. Escalate: if changes do not help, escalate to platform infra and runtime teams and attach logs: connection_trace, stream_events, and token index checkpoints.

Monitoring & SLOs (recommended)
------------------------------
- New metrics to instrument (names):
  - redwood.streaming.stream_open_total
  - redwood.streaming.stream_abort_total (labels: reason=[timeout, client_close, proxy_close])
  - redwood.streaming.resume_attempt_total
  - redwood.ingress.proxy_buffered_responses_total
  - redwood.api.dedup_id_hit_total
- Alerts to create:
  1. P0: stream_abort_rate > 0.5% over 5m for an enterprise tenant (indicative for large customers).
  2. P1: increase in resume_attempt_total by >200% (5m) without matching success.

Customer communication templates (short)
-------------------------------------
- Initial acknowledgement (within 30m):
  "Thanks — we’ve received your report and begun triage. We are reproducing the truncated stream using your request_id <id>. Short-term guidance: we can flip your tenant to non-streaming for critical paths while we stabilize. We’ll follow up with a timeline for a fix."

- Follow-up (after infra action):
  "We applied an ingress timeout increase and disabled proxy buffering for your tenant. Please retry the same request and let us know if the stream now completes. If any partial content remains, we will enable a resume flow or flip to non-streaming until an SDK patch is live."

Ownership and contact points
----------------------------
- Primary owner: Customer Success engineering (customer-success@redwood.ai).
- Platform SRE: infra-streaming-queue@redwood.ai.
- Runtime/serving: eng-serving-runtime team (pager: runtime-oncall).

Appendix: Repro curl and example headers
---------------------------------------
Minimal reproducible streaming request (curl):

curl -v \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>" \n  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \n  -H "X-Redwood-Dedup-Id: repro-<timestamp>" \n  -d '{"model":"rwd-llm-long","stream":true,"prompt":"<long prompt that produces >500 tokens>"}' \n  https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate/stream

Key headers to capture from customer:
- X-Request-Id (our correlation id)
- X-Redwood-Dedup-Id (customer supplied dedup id)
- connection_close_reason (if present in client logs)

Troubleshooting checklist (for infra):
1. Check ingress proxy logs for client connection resets and response buffer drops.
2. Inspect server-side stream_events and last_sent_token_index for request_id.
3. Temporarily set proxy_buffering off for affected route and confirm reproduction.
4. If using gRPC-web, validate that translations to gRPC preserve keepalive frames.
